Q1: Glycolic acid presents known significant hazards (Tier 1) for carcinogenicity, mutagenicity, and reproductive toxicity (CMR), oral exposure (ORL), dermal and eye contact (SKN), and organ/systemic effects (OGN). It also has expanded potential hazards (Tier 2) related to environmental impact (ENV) and inhalation (IHL), while data for endocrine disruption (EDC) is currently deficient (Tier 4).
Q2: Glycolic acid is not currently identified on specific "lists of concern." Although there is a data deficiency regarding its potential for endocrine disruption, most other hazard categories have established classifications.
Q3: Glycolic acid is extensively characterized, with approximately 28,000 literature references and a precisely defined molecular formula (C2H4O3). Its classification as a Small Molecule and lack of UVCB status further indicate a well-defined substance, with only a single hazard class currently lacking sufficient data.
